paper_title: Are Large Language Models Really Good Logical Reasoners A Comprehensive   Evaluation and Beyond
caption: The evaluation matches between LLM judge and human annotations on the 300 samples.

annotations.annotation: The bar chart illustrates the percentages of criteria met across various categories. The categories are displayed along the vertical axis, labeled from top to bottom as "No Hallucination," "Oriented," "Active," "Self-aware," "Rigorous," and "Correct." The horizontal axis represents percentage values, ranging linearly from 0% to 100% with tick labels at intervals of 20%. Each category features a stacked bar split into two sections to differentiate "Matched" and "Not Matched" components, as noted by the legend situated at the right center of the plot. The "Matched" sections, colored in a darker blue, generally cover a larger portion of each bar, with specific percentages denoted: "No Hallucination" at 98.33%, "Oriented" at 97.33%, "Active" at 97.00%, "Self-aware" at 94.00%, "Rigorous" at 95.33%, and "Correct" at 99.00%. The "Not Matched" sections, colored in a lighter blue, occupy the remaining portions: "No Hallucination" at 1.67%, "Oriented" at 2.67%, "Active" at 3.00%, "Self-aware" at 6.00%, "Rigorous" at 4.67%, and "Correct" at 1.00%. The bars are ordered without any specific sorting, and none is visually emphasized beyond the use of color.
